_comment: Shrink-only surviving-mutant ratchet for the mutation gate (issue #431).
Entries may only decrease. Raising one is a blocked change: it converts a
test-quality regression into a new normal. Enforced by
scripts/check_mutation.py; see docs/runbooks/mutation-testing.md.
PROVISIONAL. Acquired on WSL Ubuntu 22.04 / x86_64 / CPython 3.12.3 with
cosmic-ray 8.4.6 and PYTHONHASHSEED=0, NOT on the CI runner (self-hosted
Linux ARM64). The first scheduled or dispatched run of the `mutation` job
is expected to confirm these counts; if the runner reports different ones,
re-acquire there and replace this file rather than widening the entries.
Session health at acquisition: 233 mutants generated, 66 SKIPPED by
cr-filter-operators (unkillable PEP 604 annotation mutations), 167
executed, 129 KILLED, 38 SURVIVED, 0 INCOMPETENT -- 22.75% survival of
killable mutants. The unfiltered run reported 44.64%, of which 63% was
annotation noise; running without the filter re-inflates these numbers.
The same module measured on native Windows returned 233/233 INCOMPETENT
with cr-rate reporting a passing 0.00, which is why the gate checks run
health before it checks any score.
AWAITING_ACQUISITION map. Modules listed here have been added to the
target set but their survivor count has not yet been acquired on Linux.
The value is the ISO date the entry landed on `main`; scripts/check_mutation.py
fails the build if it persists past GRACE_PERIOD_DAYS (=14). The intent
is to give the next scheduled CI `mutation` job time to fill in the real
number, then to alarm loudly if that never happens. See issue #434.
app/modules/adopciones/service.py was added on 2026-08-06 (PR against #434)
with cosmic-ray 8.4.6 INCOMPETENT on native Windows blocking local
acquisition (issue #431, Finding 1). The first scheduled CI mutation run
on the Linux ARM64 runner replaces the marker.
